recommendation.text: Investigate independently pinnable Owl acquisition first, while defining owned capability/transport interfaces. If availability remains unknown, prioritize an ordinary Electron adapter feasibility investigation for an explicit feature slice; retain the other-shell route as a rewrite option. None is a proven replacement.

investigationRoute.action: Record independent Owl source/distribution/types/build interface and exact versions/hashes if obtainable; absence of such a record remains unknown.
investigationRoute.exitCriteria: A concrete independently obtainable pinned dependency with provenance/tooling, or an explicit unresolved acquisition record; packaged app presence alone is insufficient.

investigationRoute.action: Resolve retained callers and choose implementation/capability fallback for task manager, native update policy, adoption and network/IPC permissions before committing to a shell.
investigationRoute.exitCriteria: Four boundary decisions each identify receiver/caller requirements, unknowns and required positive/negative/lifecycle fixtures.

investigationRoute.action: Select an owned minimal feature slice for intermediate technical feasibility, settle its private/native dependencies and preserve host/application transport identities; resolve its dynamic options/callback lifetimes first while maintaining the complete Codex target.
investigationRoute.exitCriteria: The intermediate matrix declares tested/untested/unsupported capabilities explicitly; every uncovered full-target capability remains in the later full Codex acceptance matrix.

investigationRoute.action: Specify serialization/chunk ack, synchronous preload initialization, MessagePort ownership, destroy ordering, permission denial and platform fixtures using owned inputs before adapter implementation.
investigationRoute.exitCriteria: Fixtures state expected outputs, failures and scope; pure functions remain separate from UI/IPC integration coverage.

investigationRoute.action: After selecting a route and implementing its owned interfaces, validate one isolated startup/window/transport feature path and its failure/disposal cases on the selected runtime.
investigationRoute.exitCriteria: Actual selected runtime/ABI and behavior records match the retained slice; no original-client or whole-UI completion inferred.

investigationRoute.action: Pin independent dependencies/configuration, rebuild/package from a clean environment, then compare another version with the same capability and behavior fixtures and expand to full Codex acceptance.
investigationRoute.exitCriteria: Clean-build artifact manifests, runtime/native pins, upgrade contract results and the full Codex feature/capability acceptance matrix exist; intermediate slices or bundle beautification alone cannot close final gaps.

limitations: This is a scoped analysis decision proposal, not a recovered original architecture or an implemented port.
Only existing designated metadata/contracts were read; no fresh target scan, native reverse engineering, client/UI/model execution, authentication or personal history access.
Source-confirmed API use, public documentation match and runtime/behavior equivalence remain distinct.
Not-found-in-current-public-reference is limited to the prior fetched reference pages; it is not a proof that all runtime versions lack an implementation.
The existing fixed ten-file runtime denominator and local module proposals do not establish all runtime capabilities or complete feature ownership.
Deleting a guard, adding a function placeholder, producing a nonempty token, matching names or copying a native binary does not pass a compatibility gate.

validation.scope: Existing-record references, attribution, counts and unchanged inputs only; no new source/behavior equivalence validation.
